notes:
**Document and claims (134-1.006.note.document).** This handwritten continuation follows “près des” on scan 005. It concerns Picard champs pinned by M and N. The opening noun is cancelled and replaced above the line by “champs”. No new date, author page number, display, diagram or drawing occurs; archive pencil foliation is 63, represented as a comment. H’s page 5 is witness pagination.

**Author’s qualification and assertions (134-1.006.claim.lifting).** The author describes σ through the symmetry of L⊗L, interpreted in ₂N, and writes “Je sais prouver (sauf erreur)” that every homomorphism M→₂N comes from a suitable Picard champ. The phrase “sauf erreur” qualifies that assertion and remains in the text. He places the obstruction in Ext³(X;M,N) and says an argument “universel”/“universal” makes it vanish; no argument is supplied on this page. He then claims that sections of the third sheaf over arbitrary objects lift, calls the resulting section “ensembliste”, and claims a stronger origin from degree-two hypercohomology. These are recorded assertions, not verified existence or splitting theorems.

**Mathematics and ink (134-1.006.note.readings).** The target’s left subscript 2, Ext³, the two raised 2s, the E/underlined-F distinction, and the final argument marks were inspected. A separate conditional check shows only that an involutive self-interchange, under the additive automorphism identification, has image killed by 2; see `math_work/134-1_scan006_symmetry_check.md` and event `134-1.006.check.symmetry_torsion`. It does not establish additivity in M, realization of every homomorphism, or obstruction vanishing. No expected formula was used to choose the ink. The detached lower bar favours underlined F over E in the final formula, but both remain. The ornate H is rendered consistently as script H. The extra small mark after N and two larger closing curves are preserved even though the parenthesis count remains difficult to parse; the small mark’s first reading is a semicolon. The lifting verb is resolved to “remonte” from the low middle strokes and terminal t-e, against H’s “relève”.

**Physical states and remaining limits.** H’s note supplies the insertion of “s’obtient en” and L, so neither is counted as an H omission. The small curl after inserted “en” is separately doubtful. The cancelled nouns and capital retain uncertainty. There is no cancelled extra word across the line break between “d’autres” and “termes”, and no additional “i.e.” after “hypercohomologie”. The two small points in or beside the final formula remain doubtful because copying flecks and a reproduction-edge streak are nearby. Paired high quotation strokes are retained as double quotation marks.
